title: 3 Configuration
key_sentences: Tidewater reads its settings from a single TOML file when the server starts.
Most settings can also be overridden with environment variables, which is convenient in container deployments.
Changes to the [storage] section take effect only after a full restart; a reload signal is not enough.
Any parameter can be set through an environment variable whose name is TIDEWATER_ followed by the section and the key in capital letters.
Environment variables take precedence over values in the configuration file.
The validator exits with status 1 if it finds an unknown parameter or a value of the wrong type.

rows: Address and port on which the server accepts client connections.
Directory for queue segments and metadata.
Maximum number of simultaneous client connections.
Seconds after which an idle connection is closed.
Size at which a segment file is rolled over.
When data is flushed to disk: "always", "batch" or "interval".
How long acknowledged messages are kept.
JSON file holding the accepted client tokens.
Private key for the server certificate.
Exposes server metrics in plain text over HTTP.

code:
[server]
bind = "0.0.0.0:7420"
data_dir = "/var/lib/tidewater"
max_connections = 2048

[storage]
segment_size_mb = 256
fsync = "batch"
retention_hours = 168

[auth]
mode = "token"
token_file = "/etc/tidewater/tokens.json"

export TIDEWATER_SERVER_MAX_CONNECTIONS=4096
export TIDEWATER_STORAGE_FSYNC=always
export TIDEWATER_LOG_LEVEL=debug

$ tidewater-server check --config /etc/tidewater/tidewater.toml
config OK: 14 parameters set, 0 warnings
